parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish قرال (kral), from a South Slavic language; compare Proto-Slavic *korľь (“king”) (Serbo-Croatian krȃlj/кра̑љ, Bulgarian крал (kral), Slovene králj). Ultimately from Old High German Karl, name of the Frankish ruler Charlemagne.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پلاچقه (plâçka), borrowed from South Slavic languages, perhaps via Albanian plaçkë (“loot, booty”). See also Bulgarian пля́чка (pljáčka), Romanian pleașcă and Serbo-Croatian pljȁčka /пља̏чка.
From Ottoman Turkish وشنه (vişne), from a South Slavic language, ultimately Proto-Slavic *višьňa. Doublet of ökse.
